marrow__ANAT_CH45_Q015.takeaway: A clamp in the transverse pericardial sinus passes behind the aorta and pulmonary trunk, allowing these arterial outflows to be occluded.
marrow__ANAT_CH45_Q015.displayText:
A clamp in the transverse pericardial sinus passes behind the aorta and pulmonary trunk, allowing these arterial outflows to be occluded.

Passing a clamp through the transverse pericardial sinus allows occlusion/diversion of the aorta and pulmonary trunk. The transverse sinus separates the arterial end of the heart from the venous end: the aorta and pulmonary trunk lie anterior to the sinus and the superior vena cava lies posteriorly.
emphasis: A clamp in the transverse pericardial sinus passes behind the aorta and pulmonary trunk, allowing these arterial outflows to be occluded

rationales.a: The SVC and IVC enter the right atrium posterior to the sinus, so the clamp does not loop behind both.
rationales.b: Pulmonary veins return blood to the left atrium and lie behind the clamp route.
rationales.d: SVC and pulmonary veins are not both in front of the transverse sinus.

marrow__ANAT_CH45_Q016.takeaway: Coronary dominance is determined by which artery gives rise to the posterior interventricular (PDA) artery.
marrow__ANAT_CH45_Q016.displayText:
Coronary dominance is determined by which artery gives rise to the posterior interventricular (PDA) artery.

Coronary dominance is determined by the artery that gives rise to the posterior interventricular artery. The source states that in about 65% the posterior interventricular artery arises from the right coronary artery (right dominance), in about 10% from the left coronary/circumflex system (left dominance), and in the remaining cases both systems contribute (balanced dominance).
emphasis: Coronary dominance is determined by which artery gives rise to the posterior interventricular (PDA) artery

rationales.b: The anterior interventricular artery (LAD) supplies anterior septum but does not define dominance.
rationales.c: The circumflex defines left dominance only when it gives rise to PDA; the determining vessel is PDA itself.
rationales.d: RCA often gives PDA in right dominance, but the criterion is the artery supplying PDA.

marrow__ANAT_CH45_Q017.takeaway: A posterior interventricular artery arising from circumflex defines left-dominant coronary circulation.
marrow__ANAT_CH45_Q017.displayText:
A posterior interventricular artery arising from circumflex defines left-dominant coronary circulation.

If the posterior interventricular artery arises from the circumflex branch of the left coronary artery, the circulation is left dominant. The source again notes the approximate patterns: about 65% right dominance and about 10% left dominance.
emphasis: A posterior interventricular artery arising from circumflex defines left-dominant coronary circulation

rationales.a: Right dominance means PDA arises from RCA.
rationales.c: Balanced circulation generally involves contributions from both coronary systems, not this circumflex origin.
rationales.d: The standard classification is left dominant for PDA from circumflex.

marrow__ANAT_CH45_Q018.takeaway: The circumflex artery is a branch of the left coronary artery, not the right coronary artery.
marrow__ANAT_CH45_Q018.displayText:
The circumflex artery is a branch of the left coronary artery, not the right coronary artery.

The right coronary artery does not give rise to the circumflex coronary artery. It arises from the anterior aortic sinus (right coronary sinus) of the ascending aorta, passes anteriorly and then descends in the coronary sulcus between the right atrium and right ventricle, and turns posteriorly at the inferior margin onto the diaphragmatic surface/base. Its diameter is less than that of the left coronary artery and the right conal artery is usually its first branch. The source explicitly states that the circumflex coronary artery is a branch of the left coronary artery and is the 'exclusive supplier to the right bundle branch'; this source wording is preserved as printed.
emphasis: The circumflex artery is a branch of the left coronary artery, not the right coronary artery

rationales.a: The RCA is often smaller in diameter than the left main coronary artery.
rationales.b: The RCA arises from the right (anterior) aortic sinus.
rationales.d: The right conal artery is commonly an early branch of the RCA.

marrow__ANAT_CH45_Q019.takeaway: A circumflex artery obstruction remains independent of a proximal RCA block and can continue supplying its territory.
marrow__ANAT_CH45_Q019.displayText:
A circumflex artery obstruction remains independent of a proximal RCA block and can continue supplying its territory.

The circumflex artery is a branch of the left coronary artery and therefore is not directly affected by a right-coronary-artery blockage. The source lists branches of the right coronary artery as the right conal artery, artery to the SA node, acute right marginal artery, posterior interventricular artery in the majority, and atrial/anterior/posterior ventricular branches.
emphasis: A circumflex artery obstruction remains independent of a proximal RCA block and can continue supplying its territory

rationales.a: Acute marginal branches arise from RCA, so their flow may be affected by an RCA block.
rationales.b: PDA commonly arises from RCA in right-dominant circulation and may be affected.
rationales.c: The SA nodal artery often arises from RCA and can be affected.

marrow__ANAT_CH45_Q020.takeaway: The right ventricle is not supplied by the diagonal artery, which branches from LAD to supply left-ventricular myocardium.
marrow__ANAT_CH45_Q020.displayText:
The right ventricle is not supplied by the diagonal artery, which branches from LAD to supply left-ventricular myocardium.

The marked structure is the right ventricle. The diagonal artery does not supply it; the diagonal artery is a branch of the anterior interventricular artery and supplies the left ventricle. The right ventricle is supplied predominantly by the right coronary artery and its marginal branch, while the anterior interventricular artery gives one or two anterior right-ventricular branches.
emphasis: The right ventricle is not supplied by the diagonal artery, which branches from LAD to supply left-ventricular myocardium

rationales.a: RCA contributes branches to the right ventricle.
rationales.b: LAD gives anterior right-ventricular branches as well as left-ventricular supply.
rationales.c: The acute marginal branch supplies the right ventricle.

marrow__ANAT_CH45_Q021.takeaway: The anterior interventricular (LAD) artery is a branch of the left coronary artery.
marrow__ANAT_CH45_Q021.displayText:
The anterior interventricular (LAD) artery is a branch of the left coronary artery.

The anterior interventricular artery (left anterior descending artery) is a terminal branch of the left coronary artery. The left coronary artery arises from the left aortic sinus/left posterior sinus, passes between the pulmonary trunk and left auricle in the coronary sulcus, and divides into the anterior interventricular artery and circumflex artery. The circumflex gives the left marginal/obtuse marginal branch supplying the left ventricle.
emphasis: The anterior interventricular (LAD) artery is a branch of the left coronary artery

rationales.a: The RCA supplies right heart and often posterior septum.
rationales.c: Circumflex is the other main branch of the left coronary artery; it is not the parent of LAD.
rationales.d: LAD is the artery itself, not its parent branch.

audit.tablesAndFigures: Retained by unchanged native structuredExplanation and source figure metadata.

marrow__ANAT_CH45_Q022.takeaway: The left coronary system, especially LAD, supplies the anterior two-thirds of the interventricular septum.
marrow__ANAT_CH45_Q022.displayText:
The left coronary system, especially LAD, supplies the anterior two-thirds of the interventricular septum.

The anterior two-thirds of the interventricular septum is supplied by the left coronary artery through its anterior interventricular branch. The source contrasts right-coronary distribution (right atrium, most right ventricle, variable diaphragmatic left ventricle, posteroinferior one-third of the interventricular septum, part of left atrium and conduction tissue) with left-coronary distribution (left atrium, left ventricle, a narrow strip of right ventricle and the anterior two-thirds of the interventricular septum).
emphasis: The left coronary system, especially LAD, supplies the anterior two-thirds of the interventricular septum

rationales.a: RCA usually supplies the posterior third of septum through PDA.
rationales.c: PDA supplies posterior septum, not the anterior two-thirds.
rationales.d: Circumflex supplies lateral left ventricle rather than the anterior septum.

audit.tablesAndFigures: Retained by unchanged native structuredExplanation and source figure metadata.

marrow__ANAT_CH45_Q023.takeaway: The triangle of Koch is usually supplied by a small branch of the right coronary artery.
marrow__ANAT_CH45_Q023.displayText:
The triangle of Koch is usually supplied by a small branch of the right coronary artery.

The blue dotted outline marks the triangle of Koch. In the majority of individuals its arterial supply is derived from the right coronary artery.
emphasis: The triangle of Koch is usually supplied by a small branch of the right coronary artery

rationales.b: Left coronary artery is not the usual arterial supply to the triangle of Koch in the source.
rationales.c: LAD supplies anterior septum and left ventricle rather than the nodal triangle.
rationales.d: A branch from left posterior aortic sinus is not the usual source described.

marrow__ANAT_CH45_Q024.takeaway: LAD obstruction most commonly infarcts the anterior wall of the left ventricle and anterior septum.
marrow__ANAT_CH45_Q024.displayText:
LAD obstruction most commonly infarcts the anterior wall of the left ventricle and anterior septum.

Occlusion of the left anterior descending/anterior interventricular artery causes infarction of the anterior wall of the left ventricle. The artery supplies the anterior two-thirds of the interventricular septum and adjacent anterior left-ventricular wall. The source notes that the posterior interventricular artery supplies the posterior septum and inferior right ventricle, while the circumflex artery supplies the left lateral surface.
emphasis: LAD obstruction most commonly infarcts the anterior wall of the left ventricle and anterior septum

rationales.a: Posterior septum is usually supplied by posterior interventricular artery.
rationales.c: Lateral heart is principally supplied by circumflex branches.
rationales.d: Inferior right ventricle is usually supplied by RCA/marginal branches.

marrow__ANAT_CH45_Q025.takeaway: Anterior cardiac veins drain directly into the right atrium rather than the coronary sinus.
marrow__ANAT_CH45_Q025.displayText:
Anterior cardiac veins drain directly into the right atrium rather than the coronary sinus.

The anterior cardiac vein is not a tributary of the coronary sinus; it drains directly into the right atrium. The source lists tributaries of the coronary sinus as the great cardiac vein, middle cardiac vein, small cardiac vein, posterior cardiac vein and oblique vein of the left atrium. Thebesian veins/venae cordis minimae, anterior cardiac veins and the right marginal vein drain directly into the right atrium.
emphasis: Anterior cardiac veins drain directly into the right atrium rather than the coronary sinus

rationales.a: Posterior cardiac veins commonly drain to the coronary sinus.
rationales.b: Small cardiac vein is a coronary sinus tributary.
rationales.d: Great cardiac vein drains into the coronary sinus.

marrow__ANAT_CH45_Q026.takeaway: The great cardiac vein accompanies the LAD in the anterior interventricular groove before turning into the coronary sulcus.
marrow__ANAT_CH45_Q026.displayText:
The great cardiac vein accompanies the LAD in the anterior interventricular groove before turning into the coronary sulcus.

The great cardiac vein lies in the anterior interventricular sulcus. It begins at the cardiac apex, ascends in the anterior interventricular groove to the atrioventricular groove, then passes leftward and posteriorly to enter the coronary sinus at its origin. It accompanies the anterior interventricular artery (left anterior descending artery).
emphasis: The great cardiac vein accompanies the LAD in the anterior interventricular groove before turning into the coronary sulcus

rationales.a: It later enters the anterior coronary sulcus but begins beside LAD.
rationales.b: Posterior right coronary sulcus is associated with small cardiac vein/coronary sinus.
rationales.d: Middle cardiac vein accompanies the posterior interventricular artery in the posterior groove.

audit.tablesAndFigures: Retained by unchanged native structuredExplanation and source figure metadata.

marrow__ANAT_CH45_Q027.takeaway: The coronary sinus lies posteriorly in the AV groove and empties into the right atrium.
marrow__ANAT_CH45_Q027.displayText:
The coronary sinus lies posteriorly in the AV groove and empties into the right atrium.

The coronary sinus ends in the right atrium. It develops from the left horn of the sinus venosus and lies in the posterior part of the atrioventricular groove. It opens into the right atrium between the opening of the inferior vena cava and the right atrioventricular orifice. Venae cordis minimae drain directly into the nearest heart chamber and can open into all four chambers.
emphasis: The coronary sinus lies posteriorly in the AV groove and empties into the right atrium

rationales.a: It occupies the posterior, not anterior, part of the coronary sulcus.
rationales.c: Venae cordis minimae empty directly into chambers rather than into coronary sinus.
rationales.d: The coronary sinus develops from the left horn of the sinus venosus.

audit.tablesAndFigures: Retained by unchanged native structuredExplanation and source figure metadata.

marrow__ANAT_CH45_Q028.takeaway: The middle cardiac vein accompanies the posterior descending artery in the posterior interventricular groove.
marrow__ANAT_CH45_Q028.displayText:
The middle cardiac vein accompanies the posterior descending artery in the posterior interventricular groove.

The middle cardiac vein lies in the posterior interventricular groove accompanying the posterior descending/posterior interventricular artery and is therefore most likely to be injured while exposing that artery.
emphasis: The middle cardiac vein accompanies the posterior descending artery in the posterior interventricular groove

rationales.a: Great cardiac vein accompanies LAD in the anterior interventricular groove.
rationales.b: Posterior vein of left ventricle drains posterior LV but does not closely accompany PDA.
rationales.c: Small cardiac vein follows the right margin and posterior AV groove.
